# Port Daddy Docs for LLMs

Port Daddy is a local-first multi-agent coordination daemon. Use these canonical URLs when summarizing the product, docs, API, tutorials, integrations, and operational guidance.

Canonical site: https://portdaddy.dev/
Sitemap: https://portdaddy.dev/sitemap.xml

## Primary Entry Points

- [Port Daddy - Local Coordination for AI Coding Agents](https://portdaddy.dev/): Port Daddy is a local app and background service that helps AI coding agents share notes, claim work, avoid collisions, recover interrupted runs, and show what is happening on your machine.
- [Docs Overview - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/docs): Start here, learn what Port Daddy does, install it, then jump to runnable examples or reference.
- [Quickstart - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/docs/quickstart): Install Port Daddy, check the local service, claim a port, and start the first coordinated agent task.
- [Start Here - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/docs/get-started): The canonical first-run path: install Port Daddy, verify the daemon, open the app, and run one named session.
- [Best Practices - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/docs/best-practices): Keep agent work visible, avoid collisions, recover interrupted runs, and promote changes safely.
- [API Reference - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/docs/api): Inspect Port Daddy API routes, request shapes, response contracts, and the workflows they support.
- [Skill + MCP for AI Agents - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/mcp): Use the Port Daddy agent skill and MCP server together: an instruction manual plus callable tools for sessions, claims, scoped channels, inboxes, readiness, salvage, fleets, and handoffs.
- [Tutorials - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials): Follow hands-on Port Daddy tutorials from first install through sessions, DNS, tunnels, fleet YAML, messaging, and background agents.
- [Integrations - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations): Wire Port Daddy into Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, LangChain, CrewAI, Aider, Continue.dev, and other developer tooling.
- [Executable Examples - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/examples): Run complete Port Daddy example programs for browser buttons, test reporters, editor commands, and webhook adapters that talk to local agents.
- [Blog - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog): Read current Port Daddy field notes about FleetBar, Fleet Control Center, launch readiness, recovery maps, PD Tube, daemon provenance, and coordination policy.
- [Whitepaper - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/whitepaper): Read the technical whitepaper behind Port Daddy: local-first agent coordination, signed identity, locks, sessions, and recoverable work.
- [The Anchor Protocol - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/whitepaper/anchor-protocol): Read the Anchor Protocol paper inline with a guided explanation of scoped identity, delegation, verification, and why it matters for Port Daddy harbors.
- [The Bonded Commons - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/whitepaper/bonded-commons): Read the Bonded Commons paper inline with a guided explanation of evidence trails, advisory claims, collateralized work, and the future agent economy Port Daddy can support.

## Tutorials

- [Tutorials - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials): Follow hands-on Port Daddy tutorials from first install through sessions, DNS, tunnels, fleet YAML, messaging, and background agents.
- [Run Event-Triggered Agents - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/always-on): Combine pd spawn and pd watch so agents react to channel events automatically across Ollama, Codex, Claude, Gemini, Aider, and custom backends.
- [Debug Coordination Failures - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/debugging): Use harbor activity, notes, ownership, diagnostics, and session history to find the exact point where work drifted.
- [Resolve Services by Name - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/dns): Register harbor-local service names so agents and scripts can discover endpoints without hardcoded addresses.
- [Run Background Fleets - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/fleet): Declare background agents in YAML, bind them to project events, and keep QA, docs, and research work continuously inspectable.
- [Install the Local Control Plane - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/getting-started): Install the daemon, open FleetBar, join the project harbor, and verify the control plane before asking agents to work.
- [Start Inside a Harbor - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/harbors): Create the project boundary first, then run agents, sessions, ports, channels, and recovery inside a named permission scope.
- [Use Agent Inboxes - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/inbox): Send direct handoffs, publish channel events, and subscribe to live SSE updates without losing attribution.
- [Map a Monorepo - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/monorepo): Scan a large repo, detect service boundaries, register them in the harbor, and bring the local stack up and down cleanly.
- [Coordinate Multiple Agents - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/multi-agent): Run two agents in the same harbor with file claims, session notes, conflict visibility, and channel signals.
- [pd spawn: Launch One-Shot Agents - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/pd-spawn): Start a bounded agent job with sessions, heartbeats, notes, cost telemetry, and salvage wired around the backend.
- [Pipe Agent Conversations - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/pd-tube): Use PD Tube to send, read, reply, and resume channel conversations as clean JSON lines for scripts and agents.
- [Use Ambient Attention Signals - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/pheromone): Attach decaying numeric signals to files, sessions, or ideas so agents can prioritize work without extra chat traffic.
- [Build Reactive Pipelines - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/pipelines): Chain channels, watchers, locks, and spawned agents into event-driven workflows with clear ownership boundaries.
- [Walk the 11 Product Primitives - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/primitives): Use the Mac app, Fleet Control Center, Shipwright, and CLI checks to see where every public primitive lives.
- [Plan Remote Coordination - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/remote-harbors): Separate what works today with tunnels and DNS from the roadmap for cross-machine daemon coordination.
- [Name Work Inside the Harbor - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/semantic-identities): Use project:stack:context names so services, agents, sessions, channels, and wildcard queries stay predictable across runs.
- [Model Session Phases - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/session-phases): Move work through planning, implementation, review, and done states with phase-aware recovery and handoff evidence.
- [Use Operator Shortcuts - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/sugar): Use pd begin, pd done, pd whoami, and pd with-lock as the daily command layer over the lower-level primitives.
- [Inspect the Activity Ledger - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/time-travel): Query the append-only event timeline. Correlate infrastructure events with agent session notes to diagnose coordination failures.
- [Expose a Local Service - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/tunnel): Publish one harbor-owned service through pd tunnel with clear ownership, explicit provider choice, and a reversible path.
- [Observe Runtime Channels - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/watch): Use pd watch to follow channel activity, inspect event pressure, and trigger bounded responses from scripts or agents.

## Examples

- [Executable Examples - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/examples): Run complete Port Daddy example programs for browser buttons, test reporters, editor commands, and webhook adapters that talk to local agents.
- [Sketch agent archetypes before you launch them - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/examples/agent-archetypes): Compare star, ring, arbiter, watchdog, and repair topologies before committing a fleet shape to YAML.
- [Build an editor lightbulb that asks the local agent - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/examples/editor-lightbulb-to-agent): Select code in a local page, publish the file and range to the agent, and render the explanation inline.
- [Claim a collision-free port for an ephemeral CI database - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/examples/ephemeral-ci-db): Give short-lived test databases clean local ports so CI helpers and agents do not collide on the same machine.
- [Elect one leader from a local agent swarm - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/examples/leader-election): Use Port Daddy locks and inboxes so one local agent becomes the coordinator while the rest remain safe followers.
- [Build WebRTC signaling over agent inboxes - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/examples/p2p-webrtc): Use durable Port Daddy inbox messages for offer-answer rendezvous before peers switch to a direct local link.
- [Build a button-to-agent loop with PD Tube - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/examples/pd-tube-button-to-agent): Turn a plain HTML button into a local phone line to the agent session already running in your project.
- [Build a test reporter that asks the agent for help - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/examples/test-failure-to-agent): Wrap a failing test command, publish the failure to the local agent, and print the diagnosis back in the terminal.
- [Build a webhook adapter backed by your workstation - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/examples/webhook-to-local-agent): Accept Slack, Discord, Linear, or generic webhook JSON and route it to the local agent through PD Tube.

## Integrations

- [Integrations - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations): Wire Port Daddy into Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, LangChain, CrewAI, Aider, Continue.dev, and other developer tooling.
- [Aider - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations/aider): CLI integration for Aider. pd begin wraps Aider sessions with automatic port assignment, notes, and salvage on crash.
- [Claude MCP Server - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations/claude-mcp): Native Model Context Protocol integration for Claude Code agents. Provides structured tools for port claiming, session management, and agent coordination.
- [Continue.dev - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations/continue-dev): IDE extension integration for Continue.dev. File claims prevent collisions when multiple Continue agents edit the same codebase.
- [CrewAI - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations/crewai): Session-per-crew-member integration for CrewAI. Each crew member gets an isolated session with file claims and coordinated notes.
- [Cursor - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations/cursor): MCP integration for Cursor IDE. Port Daddy tools appear natively in Cursor's AI assistant for seamless port and session management.
- [LangChain - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations/langchain): Python SDK wrapper for LangChain agents. Gives chains and agents access to port claiming, sessions, and pub/sub coordination.
- [Windsurf - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations/windsurf): MCP integration for Windsurf IDE. Enables AI flows to coordinate ports, sessions, and locks through Port Daddy's structured tools.

## Templates

- [Agent Templates - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/agents/templates): Use the current Port Daddy agent templates: starter fleet YAML, always-on agents, CI repair loops, event-driven ops, remote harbors, research swarms, and secure messaging primitives.

## Blog

- [Blog - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog): Read current Port Daddy field notes about FleetBar, Fleet Control Center, launch readiness, recovery maps, PD Tube, daemon provenance, and coordination policy.
- [Backend Readiness Is Dependency Truth - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/backend-readiness-is-dependency-truth): A model backend is ready only when credentials, packages, CLI auth, model catalog, and telemetry policy all agree.
- [Bond Pricing Is a Market, Not a Constant - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/bond-pricing-is-a-market): Daily budgets are training wheels. The v2 of the Bonded Commons paper points at the destination: cleanup-cost lower bounds, scope multipliers, the Bonded Advisor pattern, and Thomas Youle's competitive-insurance market.
- [The Control Plane Is the Product - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/control-plane-is-the-product): A local agent system is only trustworthy when project identity, file ownership, runtime provenance, backend readiness, cost, and recovery share one inspectable control plane.
- [Coordination Guard Turns Claims Into Policy - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/coordination-guard-claims-into-policy): Notes and file claims are useful as shared facts. Coordination Guard makes them matter at commit time.
- [Evidence That Survives Multiple Machines - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/evidence-that-survives-machines): A note that only your laptop can verify is half a record. The v2 Merkle forest, the KMS witness, and the new mutable-signal ledger turn evidence into something a CI pipeline or a teammate can verify in 700 bytes.
- [Cold Start Without Surprise Launches - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/fleet-designer-cold-start): A good first-run flow should inspect the repo, expose missing credentials, simulate the fleet, and keep the human in control before any agent starts spending money.
- [Passkey Identity Across Machines - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/passkey-identity-across-machines): Single-node scope was a true description that stopped being true. The Federated Sovereign replaces it with passkey-first identity, an abstract KMS, mobile-as-viewer, and an honest recovery story.
- [PD Tube Turns UI Events Into Agent Work - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/pd-tube-event-reply-loop): PD Tube is the small event-reply loop underneath button-to-agent examples, test reporters, editor lightbulbs, and webhook adapters.
- [Keeping the Map Honest - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/recovery-roadmap-map-truth): Roadmaps, recovery docs, session notes, and live daemon state drift unless one surface reconciles them into an operator-readable map.
- [Running Is Not the Same as Current - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/running-is-not-current): A daemon can be alive, reachable, and still serving the wrong checkout. Runtime provenance has to be visible before you trust UI or CLI behavior.
- [Telemetry Is a Launch Gate - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/telemetry-is-a-launch-gate): Operator-facing launches should not succeed unless the backend can prove exact tokens, exact rates, and persisted nonzero cost.

## White Papers

- [Whitepaper - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/whitepaper): Read the technical whitepaper behind Port Daddy: local-first agent coordination, signed identity, locks, sessions, and recoverable work.
- [The Anchor Protocol - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/whitepaper/anchor-protocol): Read the Anchor Protocol paper inline with a guided explanation of scoped identity, delegation, verification, and why it matters for Port Daddy harbors.
- [The Bonded Commons - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/whitepaper/bonded-commons): Read the Bonded Commons paper inline with a guided explanation of evidence trails, advisory claims, collateralized work, and the future agent economy Port Daddy can support.
